title: Dialer modes and pacing
blurb: Preview, progressive, power, predictive, and TCPA manual touch, with the abandon window kept honest.
summary: Five modes. The simulator is a classroom. The campaign dialog is the system of record.

lessons.title: Preview lets the agent read first
paragraphs: Preview delivers the contact and, on the product page, CRM history before the call is placed. It is the mode for conversations that need context. It does not overdial, so abandon from extra ringing lines is not the design.

The product page's Manual Touch mode goes further and removes automated dialing. Preview itself can still place the call after the agent has seen the record. Do not describe preview and TCPA manual touch as the same switch.

lessons.title: Progressive keeps one call per free agent
objectives: Check the other sentence in the UI
paragraphs: The outbound product page says progressive dialing automatically dials one customer per available agent and is what centers use when they want to avoid dropped outbound calls. The dialer product page also says progressive is appropriate when fewer than 10 agents are active, and that it adapts pace to campaign performance.

Those two sentences are both public and they are not the same sentence. One says one call per available agent. The other says the pace adapts. Reconcile them in the admin UI of your domain. This lab's simulator uses the one-call reservation so you can see abandon stay near zero.
uncertain: Five9 publishes both 'one customer per available agent' and 'adaptively control dialing pace' for progressive. This lab does not know which sentence the current build implements.

right: Fewer than 10 active agents as guidance

lessons.title: Power dials a ratio you chose
objectives: Set a power ratio on purpose
Treat the abandon warning as a brake
paragraphs: The dialer page says power dials a user-configured number of calls per available agent and adjusts from abandon rates. It points that mode at a small group with a large list. The outbound page says the same shape: a small sales team and a large prospect list.

Because you choose the lines, you can create live answers with no agent. The abandon cap and the warning on the default-settings page are the brakes. The simulator lets you move lines per agent and watch the amber abandon line.

lessons.title: Predictive fills idle time, and it can drop calls
objectives: Explain predictive without claiming the source code
paragraphs: The dialer page says predictive mode uses algorithms to predict agent availability and is suited to more than 10 active agents. The outbound page says it increases time spent talking to people instead of dialing. Both are marketing descriptions of an overdial.

The default-settings topic is the control room: monitor abandoned call percentage, a max percentage, a warning if you change the max, 30 rolling days on US domains, and 24 hours on UK domains. A community test article says predictive throttles and does not necessarily lock to one-to-one, while other lines in that same article talk about dropping to one-to-one. Use the settings page as the control. Treat the test article as a field note with mixed wording.

cites.label: Dialing modes live testing
cites.note: Community test notes. Wording inside the article is not uniform.

uncertain: The exact throttle curve is not specified on the default-settings page. The community test article disagrees with itself about an instant drop to 1:1.

lessons.title: TCPA manual touch is a typed number
paragraphs: TCPA manual touch exists only on domains enabled for it. The community article says those domains are generally for telemarketing to cell phones without express consent, and that no other dialing mode is available. Contacts are shown and not dialed. The agent must type the external number. Paste and drag-and-drop are not allowed. The Dial button enables when the typed number matches.

Preview time still exists. If it expires, the agent goes Not Ready and nothing auto-dials. Dial Immediately and Dial Number are removed. The rule also covers click-to-dial, previews, and queue or voicemail callbacks. Internal speed dial and a third-party transfer do not make you retype. There is a permission to skip records.

lessons.title: The defaults are the compliance posture
objectives: Treat the warning as part of the design
paragraphs: For every dialing mode, the default-settings topic says options start at values Five9 recommends for FCC, FTC, and UK Ofcom telemarketing rules. If you change them you can see a warning. The example field is Max Abandoned Call Percentage.

Other defaulted fields on that page include max queue time, the out-of-numbers alert, whether abandon percentage is monitored, call analysis, voice detection level, and the action when max queue time expires. Calculations differ for US and European domains. The topic tells you to refer to the current agency rules.

lessons.title: Pick a mode in one page
objectives: Match five constraints to five modes
paragraphs: Use the person's job, not the logo. Context before the call is preview. A promise of no dropped calls and a small team is progressive. A small team and a huge list, with eyes on abandon, is power. A large team whose idle time is the enemy is predictive, with dedicated agents. A cell book without consent is TCPA manual touch, and only if the domain is enabled.
The ten-agent lines on the dialer page are guidance from a product page. The abandon windows are admin-guide facts. The simulator is a classroom. Your domain's dialog is the system of record.
